anomalies.description: A sudden, large explosion occurs behind and slightly above the yellow vehicle, producing a bright orange fireball followed by a rapidly expanding plume of dark smoke and dust that engulfs the area.

A large, sudden plume of dark smoke and dust erupts directly ahead of the vehicle, consistent with a near-instantaneous blast event (e.g., IED detonation) occurring just in front of or under the lead vehicle.; Sustained expansion and dissipation of the explosion's effects: massive dust cloud engulfs the road, obscuring the lead vehicle; smoke column rises and drifts; debris and shockwave effects visible through violent dust displacement and tree movement. This is the aftermath phase of the initial blast.

A large, sustained dust and smoke plume erupts and expands in the center of the road ahead, consistent with a near-simultaneous or rapidly successive series of explosions (e.g., IED detonation). The plume rises vertically and spreads laterally, obscuring the background; no vehicle impact or collision is visible, and the pattern matches blast effects rather than fire or accident.
